comments.content:
Since `handler.ServeHTTP` no longer unwraps `response.Response` into `resp.Data`, `getStatusCode` now receives the non-nil wrapper struct instead of the payload. This changes the status code for wrapped nil payloads:
- handler returns `response.Response{Headers: ...}, err` (nil `Data`): previously the status code came from `err` (e.g. 404/500), now `isNil(data)` is false in `getStatusCode`, so it returns `207 Partial Content`.
- POST handler returns `response.Response{Data: nil}`: previously `202 Accepted`, now `201 Created`.

Unwrapping the payload for status computation preserves the previous contract while keeping the metadata in the body.

comments.content: `Metadata` is typed `interface{}`, so assigning a nil `map[string]any` (the common `response.Response{Data: ...}` case) stores a non-nil, typed-nil value in the interface. `json:"metadata,omitempty"` therefore does not omit it and clients receive `"metadata":null` on every such response (this is also what the new responder test asserts), contradicting the documented behavior in `docs/advanced-guide/setting-custom-response-headers/page.md` ("If no metadata is provided, the response only includes the data field"). Typing the field as a map makes `omitempty` behave as intended.

comments.content: This new case shadows the `resTypes.Raw` / `resTypes.File` dispatch for wrapped payloads. Before this change `handler.ServeHTTP` unwrapped `resp.Data` and then `Respond` switched on the inner value, so `response.Response{Data: response.Raw{...}, Headers: ...}` was written as raw bytes and `response.Response{Data: response.File{...}, Headers: ...}` was written with the file's content type. Now the outer `Response` matches first, so such payloads are JSON-encoded inside the envelope (`[]byte` becomes base64, file bytes are JSON, `Content-Type` is forced to `application/json`), silently breaking the documented custom-header use case for raw/file responses. Consider unwrapping the wrapper before the switch (capture `v.Metadata`/`errorObj`, then dispatch `v.Data` through the existing `Raw`/`File`/default cases) instead of handling it as a dedicated case.
